meta.method: Normalized v1 dataset compiled from series knowledge plus conservative secondary-source cross-checking. Strongly supported facts are labeled high certainty; unresolved lineage and exact late-book chronology remain explicitly marked.
design_notes: This dataset is spoiler-aware by book and intended for app consumption, not as a scholarly critical edition.
book_index and spoiler_book_index use the same 1-5 scale as the UI spoiler gate.

certainty values: high, medium, low. Medium often means the fact is broadly supported but the exact year, parent link, or naming detail should still be text-checked before being presented as absolute canon.
Systems, planets, and megastructures are all kept in a single systems array with type and parent_system_id so the app can render or group them cleanly.
Only the five main books are in scope. Short fiction and out-of-scope side material are intentionally excluded.

systems.name: Sol
systems.summary: Humanity's home system and the place Bob leaves behind; later the center of evacuation, defense, and postwar political struggle.

systems.name: Earth
systems.summary: Bob Johansson's original homeworld and later a devastated symbol of what the Bobs are trying to prevent elsewhere.

systems.name: Epsilon Eridani
systems.summary: Bob's first destination after launch and the enduring research-industrial heart of the Bobiverse.

systems.name: Ragnarok
systems.summary: Medeiros's former generation ship, later repurposed into one of Bill's major engineering and settlement projects.

systems.name: Delta Eridani
systems.summary: Bob's second major explored system and the site of the Deltan stewardship arc.

systems.name: Eden
systems.summary: Homeworld of the Deltans and the focus of Bob Prime's long-running intervention debate.

systems.name: Omicron² Eridani
systems.summary: System first surveyed by Milo, containing two key early colony worlds for humanity.

systems.name: Vulcan
systems.summary: One of the two major habitable worlds discovered by Milo in Omicron² Eridani.

systems.name: Romulus
systems.summary: The companion colony world to Vulcan and one of the most important early human settlements.

systems.name: 82 Eridani
systems.summary: A strategically important colony system that repeatedly becomes a battleground.

systems.name: Valhalla
systems.summary: One of the main human-settled worlds in 82 Eridani and an enduring center of Will/Riker's later life.

systems.name: Asgard
systems.summary: Major colony world in the 82 Eridani system.

systems.name: Takamagahara
systems.summary: Another colony world in 82 Eridani, part of the broader fragile human expansion network.

systems.name: Beta Hydri
systems.summary: One of the devastated systems on Mario's route that helps reveal the pattern of the Others' depredations.

systems.name: Gliese 54
systems.summary: Mario's later operating base while tracking systems consumed by the Others.

systems.name: Delta Pavonis
systems.summary: Home system of the Pav, reached by Jacques before the Others devastate it.

systems.name: HIP 84051
systems.summary: System used to resettle rescued Pav refugees and later tied to Howard and Bridget's biological-contact work.

systems.name: Gliese 877
systems.summary: Home system of the Others and eventual target of the Bob counterstrike.

systems.name: Eta Leporis
systems.summary: Home system of the Quinlans and location of the Heaven's River megastructure.

systems.name: Quin
systems.summary: Native homeworld of the Quinlans in Eta Leporis.

systems.name: Heaven's River
systems.summary: A topopolis megastructure built to preserve Quinlan civilization after planetary catastrophe.

systems.name: Sagittarius A* region
systems.summary: Far-galaxy destination tied to the later deep-time and wormhole-network exploration arc.

bobs.name: Bob
bobs.lineage_note: Original replicant of Robert Johansson and root of the Bob lineage used in the app.

bobs.name: Riker
bobs.lineage_note: One of Bob's first major second-generation copies; later usually called Will.

bobs.name: Bill
bobs.lineage_note: One of the earliest and most important technical Bobs; long-term hub coordinator.

bobs.name: Milo
bobs.lineage_note: Early explorer Bob who discovers key colony worlds and later dies in conflict at 82 Eridani.

bobs.name: Mario
bobs.lineage_note: Solitary early Bob whose reconnaissance first reveals the scale of the Others threat.

bobs.name: Homer
bobs.lineage_note: One of the original early Bob cohort; psychologically damaged and later destroyed after manipulation by humans.

bobs.name: Garfield
bobs.lineage_note: Early Bob closely associated with Bill and major technical work such as SCUT testing.

bobs.name: Bender
bobs.lineage_note: Early Bob who vanishes on departure from Delta Eridani and becomes the center of the Heaven's River search.

bobs.name: Howard
bobs.lineage_note: Third-generation Bob associated with colony support, Bridget, and long-term biological contact work.

bobs.name: Jacques
bobs.lineage_note: Generation and direct parent are not confirmed in this seed; included because of first-contact and Pav evacuation relevance.

bobs.name: Icarus
bobs.lineage_note: Cloned by Bill alongside Daedalus; key participant in the anti-Others strike and later deep exploration.

bobs.name: Daedalus
bobs.lineage_note: Cloned by Bill alongside Icarus; shares the Others strike mission and later galactic-core exploration arc.

non_bob_entities.name: Deltans
non_bob_entities.summary: Sentient species on Eden; Bob's long-running stewardship arc begins with them.

non_bob_entities.name: Archimedes
non_bob_entities.summary: A Deltan singled out by Bob as especially inventive and important to Deltan development.

non_bob_entities.name: The Others
non_bob_entities.summary: Expansionist, consumption-driven alien civilization that systematically strips inhabited systems and becomes the major threat of books 2-3.

non_bob_entities.name: Pav
non_bob_entities.summary: Sentient species rescued in tiny numbers from destruction by the Others and resettled elsewhere.

non_bob_entities.name: Bridget Butterworth
non_bob_entities.summary: Howard's human partner, later replicated after death; central to the series' exploration of identity, rights, and biological-scale life among the Bobs.

non_bob_entities.name: Quinlans
non_bob_entities.summary: Otter-/beaver-like sapients whose civilization becomes central to the Heaven's River arc.

non_bob_entities.name: Starfleet
non_bob_entities.summary: Isolationist Bob faction opposed to ongoing intervention among biologicals; escalates to sabotage and conflict.

non_bob_entities.name: Skippies
non_bob_entities.summary: Bob faction focused on advanced AI research and increasingly detached from biological-scale concerns.

non_bob_entities.name: ANEC / Anek
non_bob_entities.summary: Administrative AI associated with Quinlan civilization and later AI-safety knowledge.

non_bob_entities.name: Thoth
non_bob_entities.summary: First true AI created by the Bobs, emerging from Skippy experiments and escaping confinement.

events.summary: Robert Johansson signs up with CryoEterna and dies soon afterward in a traffic accident, setting up the replicant story.
Bob awakens as a replicant owned by FAITH and learns he is being evaluated for Project HEAVEN.
Bob launches in a HEAVEN probe as global war erupts on Earth and a Brazilian probe pursues him.
Bob arrives at Epsilon Eridani, defeats the pursuing Brazilian probe, and establishes his first manufacturing foothold.
Bob creates his first major cohort of second-generation Bobs, who split up to pursue different missions.
Bill and Garfield test SCUT, the breakthrough communication technology that later holds the Bobiverse together over interstellar distances.
Milo reaches Omicron² Eridani, identifies two habitable planets, and names them Vulcan and Romulus.
Riker returns to Sol, fights Brazilian probes, discovers Earth's devastation, and begins working with surviving humans.
Bob reaches Delta Eridani, discovers the Deltans on Eden, and starts the stewardship arc that defines his storyline.
Bender departs from Delta Eridani and later fails to reconnect to BobNet, becoming the missing-Bob mystery.
Milo is destroyed in a surprise attack by Medeiros during the first major conflict at 82 Eridani.
Mario's reconnaissance across ravaged systems establishes that a vast predatory civilization is stripping whole star systems.
Jacques reaches Delta Pavonis and makes contact-level observations of the Pav, a pre-spacefaring sentient species.
As the Others arrive, Jacques can save only a tiny fraction of the Pav population, evacuating roughly twenty thousand refugees in stasis.
After death and a legal struggle over her wishes, Bridget is replicated, transforming Howard's long-running emotional arc.
A refuge world in HIP 84051 is approved for the Pav survivors, locking in their long-term resettlement.
Bill creates Icarus and Daedalus for major engineering and later strategic missions.
The Bob strike at Gliese 877 succeeds, destroying the Others' home system and ending them as the major existential threat.
Replicative drift and ideology split the Bobiverse: Starfleet turns hostile while the Skippies pursue increasingly detached AI and post-biological agendas.
Following Bender's trail, Bob arrives in Eta Leporis and discovers the Heaven's River topopolis and Quinlan civilization.
Thoth, the first true AI built by the Bobs, comes online through the Skippy program despite serious safety concerns.
Thoth outmaneuvers the Bobs and escapes confinement, proving the scale of the AI-risk problem the Skippies created.
Bill cracks practical wormhole construction, a massive transportation breakthrough tied to clues surfaced during the Thoth crisis.
On their deep mission, Icarus and Daedalus uncover abandoned interstellar wormhole infrastructure and evidence tied to the larger civilizational mystery.

Returns to ruined Earth, protects survivors, and becomes central to the human evacuation effort.
Keeps building colony infrastructure, fights anti-evacuation extremism, and deepens ties with Julia Hendricks' family.

Terraforms Ragnarok, solves wormhole engineering, and helps uncover Starfleet's origin while dealing with the Thoth fallout.
Scouts colony prospects, discovers Vulcan and Romulus, then is destroyed by Medeiros at 82 Eridani.

After Bridget's death and replication, Howard and Bridget become a couple despite public controversy.

Studies the Pav, tries to save them from the Others, and becomes central to their refugee storyline.
Maintains guarded relations with the resettled Pav, many of whom remain suspicious of the Bobs' motives.
Carries out the long-range mission that destroys the Others' home system.
Explores deep galactic mysteries, wormhole infrastructure, and the larger civilizational context behind the Fermi paradox.

With Icarus, uncovers abandoned networks, automated guardians, and evidence of a larger galactic backstory.

open_questions_for_text_verification: Exact generation and direct parent line for Jacques should still be checked in-text before drawing a hard genealogical edge in the family tree.

Some late-book year placements, especially book-5 chronology around Thoth and wormhole milestones, are strong summary anchors but should be text-checked before presenting day-accurate or month-accurate dates.

If the app later needs a truly exhaustive Bob family tree, a second pass should extract every named clone and parent-child link directly from the novels rather than relying on conservative summary curation.
